query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding specific alloying elements can enhance the glass-forming ability of metallic glasses.
generation.material_initial_state: Metallic glass precursor without alloying elements.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of alloying elements such as Zr, Ti, or Cu.
generation.conditions: Controlled cooling rates during solidification and specific compositions of alloying elements.
generation.structural_mediator: The atomic structure and bonding characteristics of the alloying elements.
generation.mechanism: The alloying elements disrupt the crystallization process, promoting a more amorphous structure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased glass-forming ability leading to a wider range of compositions that can be processed into metallic glass.
generation.baseline: Metallic glass without alloying elements has a limited glass-forming ability.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to metallic glasses and may not extend to other types of materials.
generation.uncertainty: The specific effects of different alloying elements on glass-forming ability are not fully understood.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct experiments by varying the types and amounts of alloying elements in metallic glass precursors and measuring the glass-forming ability.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of alloying elements does not lead to an increase in glass-forming ability compared to the baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
